description: An end-of-unit or end-of-course judgment is expected to report a capability fairly, and steer study towards it, when it samples the capability at the outcome's level with several tasks, uses criteria and a cut set in advance, follows low-stakes practice of the same thinking, and adds no demand such as speed or anxiety that the capability lacks; no claim here tests summative assessment as a design.
title: Summative Assessment

description: For young children building a first language, frequent responsive exchanges in which an adult answers and expands the child's own turns are expected to grow the child's expressive language more than language the child only hears; one routine, dialogic shared reading, is tested against ordinary reading, and the general relationship rests on associational evidence.
title: Support Early Language Development

description: For a student whose work on a unit shows the target already done, replacing the practice they do not need with acceleration or harder enrichment, chosen from that response rather than the label, is expected to sustain progress and engagement; no claim tests this, so the page gives a labelled default design.
title: Supporting Gifted and Talented Students

description: For a student with an intellectual disability who is not yet doing an age-appropriate academic or daily-life task, teaching it in small steps with more practice, specific feedback on what the student did, functional everyday contexts and full participation in the class is expected to raise performance and participation more than lowered expectations or separate, younger-age materials, though no claim in the wiki tests this combination; neighbouring claims test mastery pacing, mnemonics, self-determination instruction, student-led IEPs and praise.
title: Supporting Students with Intellectual Disabilities
